lessons.goal_ko: 처음 만난 사람에게 어디에서 왔는지 묻고, 내가 어디에서 왔는지 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Where are you from? · I’m from ___. · Nice to meet you.

lessons.goal_ko: 이름을 묻고 말하고, 헤어질 때 인사하기
lessons.ex_en: What’s your name? · My name is ___. · See you later!

lessons.goal_ko: 안부를 묻고 내 기분을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: How are you? · I’m ___. · What about you?

lessons.goal_ko: 좋아하는 음식을 묻고 말하고, 맞장구치기
lessons.ex_en: Do you like ___? · I like ___. · Me too!

lessons.goal_ko: 원하는 것을 공손하게 달라고 하고 고맙다고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Can I have ___, please? · Here you are. · Thank you!

lessons.goal_ko: 날씨를 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: How’s the weather today? · It’s ___ today. · Take an umbrella!

lessons.goal_ko: 시계를 보고 시간을 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What time is it? · It’s ___ o’clock. · Hurry up!

lessons.goal_ko: 물건이 어디 있는지 묻고 위치(on·under)를 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Where is my ___? · It’s on / under the ___. · You’re welcome!

lessons.goal_ko: 할 수 있는 것과 없는 것을 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Can you ___? · I can ___. · I can’t ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 시간이 되는지 묻고 답하기(가상 약속)
lessons.ex_en: Are you free on ___? · Yes, I’m free. / Sorry, I’m busy. · See you on ___!

lessons.goal_ko: 하는 일을 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What do you do? · I’m a ___. · I work at a ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 일어나는 시간과 아침에 보통 하는 일 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What time do you get up? · I get up at ___. · I usually ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 가는 방법과 걸리는 시간 말하기
lessons.ex_en: How do you get to ___? · I go by ___. / I walk. · It takes ___ minutes.

lessons.goal_ko: 가격을 묻고 다른 색을 찾고 사기
lessons.ex_en: How much is this ___? · Do you have a ___ one? · I’ll take it.

lessons.goal_ko: 길을 묻고 간단히 알려 주기
lessons.ex_en: Excuse me. Where is the ___? · Go straight and turn ___. · It’s next to the ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 식당에서 주문하고 계산 요청하기
lessons.ex_en: Are you ready to order? · I’d like the ___, please. · Can I get the check, please?

lessons.goal_ko: 지난 주말에 한 일을 말하고 어땠는지 답하기
lessons.ex_en: What did you do last weekend? · I ___.(지난 일) · It was ___.

lessons.title_en: I’m going to visit my grandma.
lessons.goal_ko: 계획을 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What are you going to do this weekend? · I’m going to ___. · Have a good weekend!

lessons.title_en: Do you want to see a movie?
lessons.goal_ko: 초대하고, 수락하거나 거절하기
lessons.ex_en: Do you want to ___ with me? · Sure, I’d love to! · Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy.

lessons.goal_ko: 좋아하는 것을 말하고 이유 대기
lessons.ex_en: What’s your favorite season? · My favorite season is ___. · Because it’s ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 경험을 묻고 해 봤다·안 해 봤다고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Have you ever tried ___? · Yes, I have. · No, I’ve never tried ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 추천을 부탁하고, 추천하고, 반응하기
lessons.ex_en: Can you recommend a good ___? · You should try ___. · That sounds great!

lessons.title_en: I think the countryside is better.
lessons.goal_ko: 둘을 비교하고 내 생각과 이유 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Which is better, ___ or ___? · I think ___ is better. · It’s ___er than ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 공손하게 부탁하고, 들어주고, 고마워하기
lessons.ex_en: Could you ___, please? · Sure, no problem. · Thanks a lot. I owe you one.

lessons.goal_ko: 생각을 묻고, 말하고, 동의하거나 반대하기
lessons.ex_en: What do you think about ___? · I think ___. · I think so, too. / I don’t think so.

lessons.title_en: There’s a problem with my room.
lessons.goal_ko: 문제를 설명하고 사과에 답하기
lessons.ex_en: There’s a problem with my ___. · It doesn’t work. · I’m sorry about that.

lessons.goal_ko: 약속을 바꾸자고 하고 다른 날을 제안하거나 거절하기
lessons.ex_en: Can we change our plan? · How about ___ instead? · That works for me.

lessons.goal_ko: 어릴 때 하던 일을 묻고 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What did you use to do as a kid? · When I was a kid, I used to ___. · Did you use to ___?

lessons.goal_ko: 다녀온 여행을 말하고 어땠는지, 가장 좋았던 것 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Where did you go on your last trip? · I went to ___. · The best part was ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 좋은 소식에 축하하고 나쁜 소식에 위로하기
lessons.ex_en: Congratulations! I’m so happy for you. · That’s too bad. I’m sorry to hear that. · Guess what? ___!

lessons.title_en: What have you been up to?
lessons.goal_ko: 요즘 하는 일을 묻고, 계속해 온 일과 기간을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What have you been up to? · I’ve been ___ing lately. · How long have you been ___ing?

lessons.goal_ko: 고른 이유를 묻고 because로 이유를 말하고, 이해했다고 답하기
lessons.ex_en: Why did you choose ___? · I chose it because ___. · That makes sense.

lessons.title_en: If I were you, I’d take a break.
lessons.goal_ko: 조언을 구하고, If I were you로 조언하고, 조언에 답하기
lessons.ex_en: What should I do? · If I were you, I’d ___. · That’s a good idea.

lessons.goal_ko: 여행 중 문제를 말하고 다음 편을 묻고 표를 바꾸기
lessons.ex_en: I missed my ___. · When is the next ___? · Can I change my ticket?

lessons.goal_ko: 있었던 일을 꺼내고, 순서대로 말하고, 결말을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: You won’t believe what happened! · First, ___. Then ___. · In the end, ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 계획을 묻고, 생각 중인 계획을 말하고, 응원하기
lessons.ex_en: Do you have any plans for ___? · I’m thinking of ___ing. · I hope it works out!

lessons.goal_ko: 반품·교환을 부탁하고 문제를 말하고 환불을 요청하기
lessons.ex_en: I’d like to return this. · It’s too ___. · Can I get a refund?

lessons.goal_ko: 상대 생각을 인정하며 반대하고, 다른 안을 내고, 받아들이기
lessons.ex_en: I see your point, but ___. · What if we ___ instead? · Fair enough. Let’s do that.

lessons.title_en: I was so nervous when I started.
lessons.goal_ko: 그때 기분을 묻고 when으로 말하고, 공감하기
lessons.ex_en: How did you feel? · I was so ___ when ___. · That must have been ___.

lessons.title_en: I’d like to book a table.
lessons.goal_ko: 전화로 자리를 예약하고, 다른 시간을 묻고, 예약 이름을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: I’d like to book a table for ___. · Do you have anything at ___? · Could you put it under ___?

lessons.goal_ko: 걱정을 묻고, 걱정을 말하고, 부드럽게 도움말 주기
lessons.ex_en: What’s bothering you? · I’m worried about ___. · It might help to ___.

lessons.title_en: My most memorable trip was to Jeju.
lessons.goal_ko: 가장 기억에 남는 일을 묻고, 이유와 함께 말하고, ‘처음’이었던 경험 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What was the most memorable ___? · My most memorable ___ was ___ because ___. · It was the first time I’d ever ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 둘 중 무엇을 하겠는지 묻고, I’d rather로 고르고, 좋은 점 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Would you rather ___ or ___? · I’d rather ___ than ___. · The good thing about ___ is ___.

lessons.title_en: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake.
lessons.goal_ko: 정중하게 실수를 알리고, 무엇이 잘못됐는지 말하고, 해결을 부탁하기
lessons.ex_en: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake. · I ordered ___, but I got ___. · Would it be possible to ___?

lessons.title_en: First, you need to cut the kimchi.
lessons.goal_ko: 만드는 법을 묻고, 순서대로 설명하고, 주의할 점 말하기
lessons.ex_en: How do you make ___? · First, you need to ___. · Make sure you ___.

lessons.title_en: I should have brought an umbrella.
lessons.goal_ko: 작은 후회를 말하고, 바랐던 일을 말하고, 위로하기
lessons.ex_en: I should have ___. · I wish I had ___. · Don’t be too hard on yourself.

lessons.title_en: What would you do if you had a month off?
lessons.goal_ko: 가정해서 묻고, If I …, I’d …로 답하고, 어려운 질문에 시간 벌기
lessons.ex_en: What would you do if ___? · If I ___, I’d ___. · That’s a tough question.

lessons.title_en: I heard that it opens next Monday.
lessons.goal_ko: 소식을 꺼내고, 들은 것을 전하고, ‘듣자 하니’로 덧붙이기
lessons.ex_en: Did you hear about ___? · I heard (that) ___. · Apparently, ___.

lessons.title_en: Would you mind turning down the music?
lessons.goal_ko: Would you mind로 부탁하고, 괜찮다고 답하고, 더 정중하게 부탁하기
lessons.ex_en: Would you mind ___ing? · Not at all. · I’d appreciate it if you could ___.

lessons.title_en: He’s the kind of person who always makes people laugh.
lessons.goal_ko: 어떤 사람인지 묻고, 성격을 문장으로 묘사하고, 사이를 말하기
lessons.ex_en: What’s ___ like? · He’s the kind of person who ___. · We get along well.

lessons.goal_ko: 출처를 밝혀 소식을 전하고, 짐작을 말하고, 궁금한 점 말하기
lessons.ex_en: According to ___, ___. · It seems (that) ___. · I wonder if ___.

lessons.title_en: The main reason is that I save time.
lessons.goal_ko: 의견을 묻고, 가장 큰 이유를 말하고, 예를 들기
lessons.ex_en: What’s your take on ___? · The main reason is that ___. · For example, ___.

lessons.title_en: One advantage is that it’s fast.
lessons.goal_ko: 장점과 단점을 말하고 전체 생각으로 정리하기
lessons.ex_en: One advantage is that ___. · On the other hand, ___. · Overall, I think ___.

lessons.goal_ko: 완전히·일부만 동의하거나 조심스럽게 반대하기
lessons.ex_en: I completely agree. · I partly agree, but ___. · I’m not sure I agree.

lessons.title_en: It must be from my sister.
lessons.goal_ko: 확신 정도에 따라 추측하고(must·might), 의심을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: It must be ___. · It might be ___. · I doubt it.

lessons.goal_ko: 애매한 말의 뜻을 묻고, 내 말을 풀어 설명하고, 상대 말을 정리해 확인하기
lessons.ex_en: What do you mean by ___? · What I mean is ___. · So you’re saying ___?

lessons.title_en: I really think we should start later.
lessons.goal_ko: 강하게 제안하고, 좋은 결과를 들어 설득하고, 받아들이기
lessons.ex_en: I really think we should ___. · It would ___. · Let’s give it a try.

lessons.title_en: The problem is that the trash area is messy.
lessons.goal_ko: 문제를 짚고, 해결책을 내고, 남의 해결책에 답하기
lessons.ex_en: The problem is that ___. · One solution could be ___. · That might work.

lessons.goal_ko: 어떻게 변했는지 묻고, 변화를 말하고, 요즘 사람들 모습 말하기
lessons.ex_en: How has ___ changed? · ___ has become more ___. · These days, people ___.

lessons.title_en: In ten years, robots will probably cook.
lessons.goal_ko: 미래를 묻고, 확신 정도를 넣어 예측하고, 조건을 말하기
lessons.ex_en: Do you think ___ will ___? · In ten years, ___ will probably ___. · It depends on ___.

tasks.claim_en: Working from home is better than working at the office.
We still need to learn foreign languages, even with AI translators.
A four-day work week is a good idea.
We won’t need cash in ten years.
Package tours are better than planning your own trip.
It’s better to live in the countryside when you get older.
Children under twelve shouldn’t have smartphones.
Social media makes people less happy.
Everyone should try having a pet at least once.

L8.opener_en: Can a picture made by AI be real art?
Should popular cities limit the number of tourists?
Is it better to be a specialist or a generalist?
What can we learn from failure?
How much privacy would people give up for convenience?
Is fast fashion worth the low price?
Is space exploration worth the money?
Can money buy happiness?
Is ambition always a good thing?
Is freelance or gig work the future of jobs?
Should people eat less meat?
Is online learning as good as classroom learning?
What makes a city a great place to live?
Should a job be meaningful, or is a good salary enough?
Does technology make us more connected or more lonely?
Which jobs should never be done by robots?
What should schools teach that they don’t?
Do we buy too many things we don’t need?
What do different generations misunderstand about each other?
What will a normal workday look like in 2040?

L9.opener_en: Say the same thing to a boss, a friend, and a child.
Let’s swap idioms: tell me a Korean saying, and I’ll find an English match.
Explain a Korean pun or wordplay in English. Only if you like jokes!
Just for practice: argue that cereal is a soup.
Describe a film’s ending without spoiling it.
Turn down an invitation without sounding rude.
What’s the difference between ‘I’m fine’, ‘I’m okay’, and ‘I’m good’?
Tell a short story with a twist at the end.
‘Oh, great. Another Monday.’ What does that really mean?
Made-up meeting: your manager wants meetings at 7 a.m. Disagree politely but clearly.
Explain your job, or a hobby, in one sentence, then in three words.
Say ‘Can’t come tomorrow, sorry!’ like a formal email, out loud.
In English, ‘sorry’ isn’t always an apology. Like ‘Sorry, can you repeat that?’ What else?
Is a hot dog a sandwich? Defend your answer.
